doc.title: Al Vollmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017

title: Louis Metcalf, the Luis Russell band and Call of the Freaks
summary: Vollmer tells how he got Metcalf's children to hear their father, recalls Albert Nicholas on the Russell band, and Metcalf's role in 'The New Call of the Freaks'.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: But later at a party he was sort of divorced and he had a wife in Canada and he had some children, teenaged children. And I remember they came to the house at the party that we had and I went back to the music room and got them to come and I put on “Preaching the Blues” or whatever it was, with the Luis Russell band. What’s the guy, I’ve forgotten what it’s — “The Call of the Freaks” and I said this is your father playing and I want you to know how good your father was. So I got them to listen to their own father playing. But I have another Louis Metcalf story and that is that I cut my teeth in Sweden on the Luis Russell Band. I wanted to play a saxophone because of Charlie Holmes. I thought Higgie was the greatest trombonist ever and Henry Allen, that was one incredible band. And I remember meeting once at Ryan’s, Albert Nicholas. And I said to him, “What was it like playing in the Luis Russell band.” He said, “We all spoke the same language.” But back to Metcalf, he was the first trumpeter in the Luis Russell band and then he was replaced by Henry “Red” Allen. I heard Henry “Red” Allen, I met Henry “Red Allen but I can’t say I knew him. But anyway Louis Metcalf, Charlie Holmes said, was full of ideas, or as he pronounced them “eye-dias.” And he said he was the one who did “The Call of the Freaks.” And Luis Russell called up Louis Metcalf and said, “We’re going to go to the studio, we’re going to record your number, “The New Call of the Freaks,” and “would you like to come and be there?” So Metcalf said he did go there, he said, “I went there without my trumpet.” And he said, so he identified himself as one of the vocal trio that sings “Stick Out Your Can, Here Comes the Garbage Man.” It’s Higgy, Henry Allen and Louis Metcalf singing. And you’d never know that unless you confronted the musician himself, because he was out of the band, he was asked to come to the studio and so he was part of that studio. So those kind of things were, the detective work, has interested me.
Yeah. That’s pretty deep. Even the fact —
And it’s over for me now because they’re all gone.
I regret not having done more, not having come up with the right questions and so on, so forth, but I did what I did.
